name: Parakeet-tdt fastest+leanest on 5650U (Vulkan primary, CPU secondary)

description: Baseline: q8_0 GGUF, Vulkan primary rtf_med=0.0346 (771.5ms/22.3s), CPU 1753.8ms, RSS 978MB. WER 3.94%.

asi.dispatched_nodes: ~1440 (MUL_MAT=293 ADD=295 CONT=246 MUL=168 NORM=120 UNARY=99 CPY=72 SCALE=72 CONV_2D_DW=26 FA_EXT=24 PAD=24 IM2COL=3)
asi.model: q8_0 (fastest of bf16/q8/q5/q4 on Vulkan; WER equal within noise)

description: Vulkan fused LayerNorm+affine shader (NORM_MUL_ADD): med 770.7→744.8ms, rtf 0.0346→0.0334. Byte-identical output.

asi.change: new Vulkan shader norm_affine.comp + pipeline_norm_mul_add_f32 + can_fuse {NORM,MUL,ADD} + dispatch; fusion confirmed active (perf logger: NORM_MUL_ADD 120x)
asi.hash: sha1_12 2746b80b32fe == baseline (bit-identical numerics, same reduction order as norm.comp)
asi.hypothesis: fuse LayerNorm affine chains to remove 240 dispatches+barriers+memory round trips
asi.insight: encoder 657.8->628.7ms (-29ms); total -26ms; barrier cost per removed node ~110us confirmed but smaller than 150us estimate
asi.next: convert patch series entry 0012; then pos-bias caching (linear_pos per-T constant ~25ms), GLU fusion, GEMM tiling

description: Per-T' pos-bias caching as persistent graph inputs: med 744.8→714.9ms, long 2638.6→2526.6ms, RSS 977→973MB. Byte-identical.

asi.change: engine: per-T pos-bias cache — Encoder::compute_pos_layer one-shot + persistent ReplayGraph inputs (mark_graph_input_persistent plumbing); pe no longer registered when cached; CPU path untouched (inline)
asi.hypothesis: linear_pos(pe) is constant per T' (25.5ms GEMM/pass on medium, ~110ms on long) — cache as persistent inputs
asi.insight: med 744.8->714.9 (-30ms), long 2638.6->2526.6 (-112ms); peak_rss 977->973MB (per-layer scratch upload avoids the 183MB transient); one-time cost per T ~24 small computes+syncs
asi.pitfall: persistent inputs need upload-once + sync since scratch reused; dead pe input must not be registered (unallocated input crash in set_input)

description: cwhn depthwise-conv path + GLU cont removal: −192 nodes, med 714.9→711.5ms, byte-identical. CPU unchanged (noise).

asi.change: engine: GLU cont() removal (2 nodes/layer) + channels-first depthwise conv path (cwhn): host-transposed F16 kernels cached per layer (DwwTransposedCache) as persistent inputs, glu consumed via free reshape+permute views, output viewed [C,T] directly — kills both transpose+cont pairs (96 nodes)
asi.cpu_note: CPU med_ms noisy 1777-1914 (thermal coupling: iGPU bench precedes CPU in measure.sh); no real CPU regression from cwhn (CPU also implements cwhn natively)
asi.ggml_permute_semantics: ne[axis_i] = src->ne[i] — axis is the DESTINATION of source dim i (bit me twice)
asi.hash: byte-identical sha1_12=2746b80b32fe (cwhn shader keeps same fma tap order)
asi.hypothesis: transpose+cont pairs around dw conv cost 4 dispatches + 2 round trips per layer
asi.insight: encoder nodes 2037->1845; med 714.9->711.5 (small, partially noise); formal run noisier than quick bench (705.3)

description: Decode soup trim: gate CONT removal + argmax BLOCK=512: med 711.5→705.5ms, byte-identical.

asi.change: decode: LSTM gate CONT removal (8 dispatches/step: views are unit-stride, unary kernels take strided rows) in joint fused + prediction graphs; Vulkan argmax BLOCK_SIZE 64->512 spec constant (latency-bound GCN wave)
asi.hash: byte-identical sha1_12=2746b80b32fe (argmax tie-break order unchanged — verified by transcript hash)
asi.hypothesis: decode per-step node count and argmax latency dominate after GEMVs
asi.insight: med 711.5->705.5 formal (quick 699.8); decode node cost ~13us each in small graphs (vs ~150us in encoder: big graphs have inter-submit gaps)

description: DEAD END: coherent-loads + exec-only barriers — byte-exact-stable but slower (L1-bypass cost > flush saving). Reverted.

asi.change: experimented coherent loads (98 shader files sed) + exec-only dependency barriers (STARLING_VK_FAST_SYNC); REVERTED both
asi.finding1: hash byte-exact AND stable across 5 runs — coherent loads + exec barriers ARE deterministic on RADV/GCN (earlier no-barrier nondeterminism was overlap races + L1 staleness)
asi.finding2: SLOWER: 703-756ms vs 699.8 baseline — coherent (GLC/L1-bypass) loads cost more than the L2-flush barrier saves; mmq tile re-reads lose L1 caching
asi.hypothesis: barrier L2-flush tax (~100ms) could be avoided via coherent loads + exec-only deps
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric worse; tree restored (gate reverted; shaders checkout + norm_affine re-registered)

description: Patch-series hygiene: ggml edits formalized as 0012; re-measured baseline 699.7ms (rtf 0.0314).

asi.change: converted all live ggml-vulkan edits into patch 0012 (norm_affine.comp, argmax 512, FORCE_PIPE/FLOPS_PER_SUBMIT envs); series validates via apply_ggml_patches.sh; baseline re-confirmed after revert of the coherent-loads dead end
asi.hygiene: ggml work now survives submodule re-init; worktree state matches HEAD+series exactly

description: Kill F16→F16 weight cast copies: med 699.7→621.3ms (−11%), short −29%, byte-identical.

asi.change: skip F16->F16 ggml_cast on conv pointwise weights (GGUF already stores them F16) — was emitting 48 full-tensor CPY nodes copying ~150MB of weights per encoder pass
asi.insight: med 699.7->621.3 (-78ms, -11%!), short 351.9->251.4 (-29%!), long 2502->2439; the CPY diagnostic ([cpy] name print in STARLING_CPY_DEBUG) found it — always inspect node names not just counts
asi.pattern: ggml_cast emits CPY even for same dtype — gate every cast on actual dtype mismatch

description: DEAD END: q4_0 joint/LSTM decode weights — WER fine but no speedup (GEMV latency-bound, not bandwidth).

asi.change: custom quant: joint_net.2 + LSTM + joint.pred at q4_0, rest q8_0 (quantized from bf16-exact; recipe-based starling-quantize)
asi.finding: WER 3.64 (gate ok) but ZERO speed change (med 623.2 vs 621.3) — the n=1 decode GEMVs are latency/occupancy-bound, NOT bandwidth-bound on Vulkan dmmv; halving weight bytes does nothing
asi.hypothesis: joint vocab GEMV 141us at 39GB/s could improve with q4_0 weights (2.8MB vs 5.6MB)
asi.rollback_reason: no primary-metric gain; sha drifts (5273bfd3dbe8) for nothing; model file deleted

description: q8_0 conv pointwise weights: Vulkan flat + RSS −7% but CPU +5% — net negative, reverted.

asi.change: starling-quantize: explicit recipe rules can retype conv weights (1x1 pw as 2D matmul layout q8_0); engine skips F16 cast for quantized pw; model parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-q8pw.gguf (683MB)
asi.finding: Vulkan: med 620.7 (vs 621.3 — noise), long -17ms, peak_rss 970->903MB (-7%); WER 3.94 == baseline exactly (fixtures byte-identical transcripts)
asi.finding_cpu: CPU med 1876->1972ms (+5%): CPU prefers the F16/llamafile-sgemm path over q8_0 vec-dot for the pw matmuls
asi.hypothesis: f16 pw GEMMs at 780-815 GFLOPS vs q8_0's 950 would save ~12ms
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric flat (noise); CPU secondary regressed 95ms; net negative for the dual-target goal

description: DEAD END: exact ×0.5 fold — byte-exact, −96 nodes, but flat speed and +408MB RSS (weight copies). Reverted.

asi.change: exact ×0.5 fold of fc_factor into linear2 weights at load (q8_0 f16 block-scale halving; proven byte-exact); −96 nodes (SCALE 72→24, CPY unchanged)
asi.finding: med 628.3 vs 621.3 — NO speed change: the perf-logger's per-node times were inflated by its own timestamp+barrier; real SCALE node cost ≈ negligible. peak_rss 970→1378MB (+408): the fold COPIES 200MB of weights (mmap original stays)
asi.insight_beautiful_but_useless: power-of-2 folds are bit-exact through q8_0 scales; but node-count reductions below ~50 nodes are invisible on this workload
asi.rollback_reason: primary flat, RSS +42% — catastrophic secondary regression

description: CPU thread pinning (6 physical via STARLING_GGML_THREADS): cpu_med 1877→1582ms (−16%). Vulkan unchanged.

asi.change: STARLING_GGML_THREADS env override for the CPU backend thread count (engine feature, default unchanged at 8); measure.sh CPU leg pins 6 (physical cores)
asi.cpu_result: cpu_med_ms 1877→1582 (-16%); SMT threads hurt the ggml CPU kernels ~25% on this Zen3 (contention: 12t=2314, 8t=1973, 6t=1560-1764)
asi.hypothesis: ggml CPU kernels are memory-bandwidth/execution-port bound; SMT siblings compete

description: Final consolidated state: Vulkan rtf 0.0277 (−19.9%), CPU −10%, byte-identical, WER unchanged.

asi.final_state: Vulkan med 618ms (rtf 0.0277, -19.9% from 0.0346 baseline), CPU 1576ms (-10%), peak_rss 972MB, byte-identical transcripts (sha 2746b80b32fe), WER 3.94 == baseline
asi.quality: all wins are byte-exact — no quantization or numerics compromise was shipped
asi.session_summary: wins: LN-affine fusion (ggml patch 0012), pos-bias caching, cwhn conv, F16 cast-gating (150MB/pass of copies), decode trims, argmax block, CPU thread pinning. dead ends documented in prompt.md

description: DEAD END: forced emulated int-dot mmq — same speed as float path on GCN5. Reverted.

asi.change: experimented STARLING_VK_FORCE_INTDOT (force emulated integer-dot mmq on GCN); REVERTED
asi.finding: microbench FFN shapes: forced 717/724/630 GFLOPS vs default 741/731 — emulated dotPacked4x8EXT is NOT faster (Mesa lowers it to the same unpack+mul sequence as the float path); note device->integer_dot_product is FALSE at runtime despite the extension being exposed (banner said int dot: 0, verified by GGML_VK_DISABLE_INTEGER_DOT_PRODUCT no-op)
asi.hypothesis: emulated int-dot (unpack + v_mad_i32_i24) could beat unpack+cvt+fma float dequant

description: Stability confirmation: 620.5ms / rtf 0.0278 after all reverts. Session steady.

asi.final: steady state re-confirmed after dead-end reverts: rtf_med 0.0278, med 620.5ms, CPU 1587.9, byte-identical, WER gate green
asi.note: all experiments exhausted at current depth; remaining lever (FFN GEMM shader rewrite) documented in ideas.md

description: Wrap-up verification: engine clean, server e2e OK, byte-identical. Session total: Vulkan −19.7%, CPU −10%.

asi.final: cleanup commit verified; med 635.9 in thermal band (session best formal 618, quick 615-635 range), CPU 1615, byte-identical, WER green; end-to-end starling-serve smoke test passed (correct transcript via HTTP)
asi.thermal_note: back-to-back runs heat the APU; the formal numbers drift 615-636 depending on preceding load — all within the session's noise characterization

description: DEAD ENDS: forced split-K (parity/worse) and larger K-step decode batches (K=16 optimal as shipped). Both byte-exact.

asi.finding_splitk: GGML_VK_FORCE_SPLIT_K sweep on FFN shapes: split=2 parity (739.5 vs 735.2 GFLOPS), split=4 WORSE (643.8) — m-tiles already saturate 7 CUs; reduce-kernel overhead eats any gain; k-loop staging is not the bottleneck (ALU is)
asi.finding_kstep: STARLING_GGML_TDT_KSTEP sweep 16/24/32/48/64 on engine: K=16 best for T<=512 (643.7 vs 683-708) — the K-step graph recomputes LSTM unconditionally (no g_valid skip), so bigger K wastes more than the saved syncs; shipped defaults (16 / 96 for T>512) confirmed optimal; ALL K byte-exact (sha identical)
asi.hypothesis: skinny-GEMM split-K and bigger K-step batches would lift utilization
asi.rollback_reason: both negative-or-parity; knobs reverted (split_k env removed; KSTEP env is pre-existing engine code, untouched)
